text:
maya: dropping a new variation of the autoscale panel. focus: presets row, min/max inputs, burst toggle + duration, GPU pool picker with recommended tag, and a clearer SLO control. figma: https://redwood.mock/s/autoscale-v4.png
ben: preset chips look useful. can we add a tiny subtitle under the preset that summarizes key knobs? e.g., "Cost saver: min 0 · max 2 · burst 30s" so users know what it does before applying.
clare: agree. also the preset pills need keyboard focus styles. currently you can't tab into them with a visible indicator.
diego: on burst: suggests changing label from "Burst" to "Burst headroom" and showing the effective max GPUs in parentheses (e.g., max 4 (burst to 6)). reduces confusion about steady-state vs spike.
maya: good idea. showing computed "burst cap" inline might make the UI denser though. maybe a foldable detail line under the max field that shows it.
sam: minor copy: instead of "SLO" label use "Latency target (p99)" like jon suggested earlier. for the slider tooltip, show both ms and percentile: "p99 ≤ 500ms".
rachel: accessibility: ensure slider has aria-valuetext that reads the label + human value, e.g., "Latency target p99 500 milliseconds". thumb color: use #003f63 for contrast and add a 3px focus ring with offset.
clare: for the GPU pool dropdown, there's an a11y issue where voiceover reads the group headers twice. we should use role=group on the header container and aria-hidden on decorative text.
diego: ux question: where to surface guardrail hints (e.g., "max GPUs exceeds recommended for model"). inline under the relevant input feels more discoverable. we can also add an inline link "Why this matters" to open a side panel.
maya: plan: inline hint + a compact sticky banner at top of panel that appears only if there are any guardrail messages. banner variants: info / warning / critical depending on severity. copy suggestions welcome.
eben: (ben) banner copy proposal: "Configuration warnings — see controls below". Maybe too bland?
sam: for onboarding, show an info state: "Presets help pick reasonable defaults. You can modify any setting after applying." small question mark icon with tooltip.
rachel: keyboard behavior: ensure the min/max number inputs accept arrow up/down for increments and expose step via aria-valuenow. Also, label the unit (GPUs) with aria-label on the input.
clare: contrast on the preset chips text is borderline on dark mode. increase weight or switch to #ffffff text on the chip.
diego: telemetry ask: when a preset is applied record preset id + any manual overrides so we can see adoption.
maya: noted. acceptance criteria draft: 1) presets row with subtitle + accessible focus states, 2) collapsed detail showing burst cap when requested, 3) slider with new label and aria-valuetext, 4) GPU pool recommendations surfaced and grouped by region, 5) inline guardrail messages + sticky banner.
ben: small UX nit: change "max GPUs" label to include a help icon: "max GPUs ?" -> tooltip: "Max GPUs is the steady-state target for autoscaler."
clare: also add validation text under max if user inputs a non-integer. message: "Please enter a whole number of GPUs."
sam: for cost breakdown: prefer a separate "Burst" line item in the cost graph, not blended. ops teams asked for that.
maya: agreed, backend will need a tag on burst allocations.
deploy-bot: saved snapshot: autoscale-v4-1762100000 at 1762100005
ben: final: please ensure mobile layout stacks preset chips into a horizontally scrollable row instead of wrapping to multi-line which looks messy.
maya: thanks everyone, i'll update figma and create tickets for frontend + backend. will loop back for a quick QA pass.
